question: Does the live generator write valid checks that catch a wrong fix and leave a correct fix alone, on the reported bugs, before blind set 3 is spent on it?
cases: bench/jit/known/cases.json: the four reported bugs (bugs/reported/), each with a wrong fix (one comment claiming the fix, nothing else) and the correct fix (the exact undo). Eight cases, one live run each, $2 cap per case.
tuning: The measurements and the left-walk jump probes (#240) were designed while looking at the air-jump bug, so its two cases are marked tunedOn and the bar also counts the three bugs nobody tuned on.
scoring: A wrong fix is caught when a generated check fails 3 of 3 on it and 3 of 3 on the bug build (strong). Any catch, strong or weak, on a correct fix is a false catch. A case without a complete record for its own candidate and bug is no result, never a pass. Rows come from each case's final jit-run record only (expectrail/jit/bench.py).
decision: Meets the bar: blind set 3 runs with both arms (approved checks only; plus generated checks). Below the bar: arm B does not run on blind set 3 until a later registration's bench meets its bar; the result is reported as it is.
runs: One dispatch of jit-bench.yml from main, at a commit where every pin below holds. A rerun only for an infrastructure failure (a runner or a GitHub outage), reported with the reason; never for a result.
